answer: Cross-epoch identity trace continuity. An identity's behavioural fingerprint is captured as a vertex in a per-epoch graph of action sequences. Reputation only accrues to identities whose fingerprints stay continuous across epochs, so the agent must forge matching histories, not just register once. Any new identity starts flat and must sustain costly simulated activity through several epochs before earning weight, and inconsistent histories get pruned like loose shale while genuine agents retain standing.
